title: SMDET-selected ultracool-dwarf candidates include two objects with spectroscopically confirmed T-dwarf types
summary: The SMDET image-level neural network identified 118 previously uncatalogued high-proper-motion ultracool-dwarf candidates in WISE time-series images. Follow-up near-infrared spectra for two selected objects yielded T5 and T3 classifications, confirming their estimated spectral types within one subtype.
ai_technology: SMDET, a convolutional neural network for detecting faint moving sources in WISE time-series coadds
organization: Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 collaboration; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; California Institute of Technology/IPAC; Northern Arizona University

evidence.tested: The SMDET image-level neural network identified 118 previously uncatalogued high-proper-motion ultracool-dwarf candidates in WISE time-series images.
evidence.unknown: Most of the 118 objects remain candidates, and the study spectroscopically checks only two. Some candidates were also identified by citizen scientists, so the AI was part of a human/algorithm discovery process. The counted finding is limited to the two spectra and the candidate search result as one paper-level report.
evidence.ai_role: Scanned WISE image sequences and prioritized faint, fast-moving source candidates; researchers cross-checked catalogs, estimated photometric types and distances, and acquired spectra for two objects to verify their T-dwarf classifications.
